title: Derived universal properties of supported scalar maps
statement: Let i : D → T be a closed immersion, let R and A be commutative rings, and let φ : R → A be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Suppose ηD and ηT are maps of the ordinary constant module sheaves [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] sending, at every étale object, each constant generator r to φ(r). Then ηD on D, ηT on T, and the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of ηD (transported through the objectwise restriction-of-scalars comparison) each satisfy the unbounded derived scalar-unit universal property [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-scalar]. No flatness of A is required.

proof.text: The constant R-module sheaf is the monoidal unit, hence flat. A closed immersion is finite. For a finite i, use the jointly conservative lifted geometric stalks. The finite-stalk isomorphism identifies the stalk of i_*R_D with the finite product of the constant R-stalks. The generic point constant-sheaf isomorphism supplies these as R-modules (the same constant-germ computation as the abelian constant-stalk statement). The product is the finite free module R^E, including E empty, hence flat. The geometric-stalk flatness criterion proves flatness of i_*R_D.

proof.text: The constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction, followed by evaluation of a linear map from the rank-one free module at 1, identifies maps R_X→Res(H) and A_X→H with the same section set. The equations hD and hT at the terminal etale object and at 1 show that composition with eta_D or eta_T corresponds to the identity of this section set. The two ordinary scalar universal properties follow by composing these explicit bijections.

Apply finite_ordinary_scalar_unit to i and eta_D with the ordinary bijections from the preceding step. Its conclusion is the ordinary universal property of precisely the supported comparison in the statement.

Apply scalarUniversal_of_flat to eta_D, to its supported direct image, and to eta_T. The first step supplies their flat R-sources and the preceding two steps supply their ordinary Hom bijections. Unfold SupportedDerivedScalarUnit and assemble the three conclusions, retaining eta_D, eta_T and the specified inverse restriction comparison verbatim.
